rationale: Because xad is missing for the large majority of Compustat firms and is coalesced to zero, this expression collapses to the archive's already-tested IntangibleCapitalizedProfitability for most of the cross-section, making it a near-duplicate whose incremental information is confined to a thin advertising-reporting subsample rather than the claimed clean decomposition.

The restated-minus-reported rank wedge is a genuinely distinct construction that targets the accounting distortion rather than the profitability level, but the claim of orthogonality to profitability is overstated and the wedge is likely close to a monotone function of R&D-stock intensity scaled by earnings — i.e., at risk of rediscovering the R&D-intensity premium — so it is worth testing only with that collinearity diagnosed.

A monotone re-ranking of an existing archive signal leaves the sort, portfolios, and FF5 alpha mechanically unchanged by the proposer's own admission, so this is a cosmetic rescaling that tests estimator distribution rather than any new economic mechanism.

Replacing the ad hoc nested SUMRANK with a bounded two-way conjunction of intangible intensity and an explicit cash-flow-to-total-liabilities coverage leg is a defensible structural redesign, though it sits close to the archive's IntangibleCollateralFragility and the short leg risks being driven by the well-known distress anomaly, so the test must show incremental power over plain coverage/leverage.

Multiplying turnover and net-margin ranks is a direct restatement of the published DuPont decomposition of profitability (Soliman) and, since the product is close to a monotone recombination of ROA, the intangible-augmented denominator is a cosmetic modification of an already-tested profitability construct rather than a new mechanism.

With xad missing for most firms and coalesced to zero, the expression degenerates to three-year average ROA across the bulk of the sample, so the signal will chiefly rediscover the profitability anomaly rather than isolate a brand-capital restatement, and advertising-capital pricing is itself a published effect.
